signals.name: Stanley Druckenmiller
signals.latest_title: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Warns of an AI Earnings Bubble as Financing Costs Rise
signals.summary: Druckenmiller warned that AI infrastructure spending can generate exceptional supplier profits without guaranteeing they endure, and flagged rising financing/borrowing costs underneath the AI capex boom.
signals.connection: Directly feeds the rate-hike-odds/shutdown/jobs-week story and the broader Markets and Digital Finance concern about AI-driven credit and earnings fragility.

signals.name: Byrne Hobart
signals.latest_title: Generative video will make it harder to trust random videos
signals.summary: In a recent free issue of The Diff, Hobart argues generative video's rise is actually beneficial because society over-trusts video as a medium and needs to recalibrate.
signals.connection: Touches AI Regulation & Governance and trust/verification themes adjacent to today's OpenAI agent-misuse and EU AI Act inspection stories.

signals.name: Ben Thompson
signals.summary: Thompson's week wraps Meta vs. Amazon competitive dynamics, GM's capitulation to Apple CarPlay, and (in a companion piece) how Meta needs Walmart to help it outlast Amazon while Expedia clings to its middleware position and Google's positioning looks increasingly uncertain.
signals.connection: Applied Tech & Industry power struggle among platform aggregators, relevant background to how AI-driven commerce and ad platforms are consolidating power under US Policy & Power scrutiny.

signals.name: Packy McCormick
signals.summary: McCormick's weekly roundup covers Vironexis, Solcoa, Terraform, Joby, and Meta VR glasses; a companion piece asks whether he'd send his kids to an AI-driven alternative school (HAA), and on X he cheered a stablecoin infrastructure play (Bastion).
signals.connection: Optimist counter-read to today's AI/energy/defense anxieties, and the Bastion stablecoin nod ties into Digital Finance.

signals.name: Lenny Rachitsky
signals.latest_title: The grief, loneliness, and burnout sweeping through the tech industry right now | Molly Graham
signals.summary: Molly Graham revisits her career advice for the AI era and argues delegating work to an AI agent is nothing like delegating to a human, amid a broader burnout wave in tech; a companion post also has Lenny's blind taste-test of Opus 5.5 vs. GPT-6 Sol across coding and agentic tasks.
signals.connection: Labor & Workforce angle on AI-driven burnout and management, plus a direct Frontier Tech/AI model-comparison data point relevant to the OpenAI agent-misuse story.
